subject: Clarify indemnity offsets / notice windows for Polaris MSA redlines
messages:
From: Jason Meyer <procurement@polaris-data.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@polaris-data.com (Ellen Park)
Date: 2025-05-06T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Polaris redlines — indemnity / insurance offsets

Marcus — attaching our redline of the MSA and order form. Key asks: limit Redwood's IP indemnity only to direct infringement of customer-provided content, add an umbrella-insurance offset (we want primary + umbrella to step down Redwood's exposure), and require a 90-day notice window for third-party claims so we can marshal counsel.

Can you confirm Redwood can accept primary+umbrella offsets and provide a sample proof-of-insurance (POI) template? Also flag if any of our proposed carve-ins are a hard blocker for you.

Attachments: Polaris_MSARedline_v1.pdf (pdf), Polaris_OrderForm_comments.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks,
Jason Meyer
SVP, Procurement — Polaris Data
procurement@polaris-data.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Jason Meyer <procurement@polaris-data.com>
Cc: legal@polaris-data.com (Ellen Park), Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-06T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Polaris redlines — indemnity / insurance offsets

Jason — thanks for the redline and summary. Looping in Kimberly (Legal) and Ben (Account lead). A few quick notes from product/sales ops standpoint: we want to avoid open-ended exposure for model outputs and keep defense control where Redwood has to step in only for vendor-originating claims.

Kimberly / Ben: can you review their proposed umbrella offset language and the 90-day notice request? Two specific asks we should answer back with:
- Can we accept offsets from customer-side primary + umbrella carriers, and if so, how do we memorialize the stacking/priority?
- Is a 90-day notice period workable or do we counter with a shorter "notice slab" (proposal below)?

Proposal (drafted quickly for discussion):
- Notice slab: prompt notice on receipt of claim; if Customer fails to give written notice within 60 days after becoming aware, Redwood's obligation limited to reasonably demonstrable prejudice.
- Offsets: permit Customer's insurance to satisfy Redwood's indemnity obligations but limit recovery to amounts actually recovered by Redwood after reasonable collection efforts; Redwood to provide notice of any recoveries and account for offsets.

If Kimberly concurs, we can propose a tracked-change section and offer our POI template. Suggest a 30-min call tomorrow with Polaris legal + our legal to walk the offset mechanics.

Onward —Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jason Meyer <procurement@polaris-data.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-06T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Polaris redlines — indemnity / insurance offsets

Jason / Marcus — thanks, Jason, for the detailed markups. High level legal view and suggested redline language below. I focused on three pain points: 1) trigger clarity for IP infringement; 2) insurance offsets stacking; 3) defense control & evidence obligations.

1) Trigger: narrow to (a) third-party claim that the Redwood-supplied Service or Model directly infringes a third party's patents/copyrights, excluding Customer-provided data/prompts and Customer derivative outputs. Suggested sentence: "Redwood's indemnity obligation shall apply only to claims alleging direct infringement by the unmodified Service as provided by Redwood to Customer."

2) Insurance offsets: we can accept a reduction for recoveries from Customer's carriers, but we must preserve our right to pursue defense and recovery. Suggested mechanics: "Any amounts paid by Customer's insurers shall reduce Redwood's indemnity obligations dollar-for-dollar, provided Redwood is named as an additional insured or provided the insurer's written confirmation that proceeds are available for reimbursement; Redwood shall apply commercially reasonable efforts to collect and shall credit Customer only for amounts actually collected."

3) Notice slab / evidence window: 90 days is long; operationally we prefer a 60-day written notice window plus an affirmative "evidence manifest" requirement: Customer must produce the complaint, service, and any material evidence within 45 days of notice, and must preserve relevant custodial material. If Customer misses the 60-day notice, Redwood's obligations limited to demonstrable prejudice.

4) Defense control: Redwood will offer counsel in any defense, but for IP claims we propose a rebuttable presumption that Redwood may reasonably assume defense control where the claim implicates our model or runtime. If Customer elects to control, Redwood can reserve the right to appoint counsel at Customer expense where conflicts arise.

I will prepare a tracked redline for the MSA and an explanatory memo for the offset mechanics. Ben — please flag any commercial concessions we should include (credits, indemnity cap movement) if Polaris insists on the 90-day notice and broad output coverage.

Kimberly Park
Associate General Counsel — Redwood Inference

From: Ellen Park <legal@polaris-data.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Jason Meyer <procurement@polaris-data.com>
Date: 2025-05-08T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Polaris redlines — indemnity / insurance offsets

Kimberly / Marcus — appreciate the quick turnaround and the proposed language. A few replies:

- Polaris can name Redwood as an additional insured for claims covered by our policies; we'll work with our broker to provide written confirmation.
- The "evidence manifest" asks are acceptable provided Redwood commits to preserving logs and making a reasonable evidence request within 30 days of receiving the complaint.
- On notice: we can move the formal written notice from 90 to 75 days as a compromise, but we need a hard acceptance that Customer outputs remain actionable (we cannot accept language that broadly immunizes outputs from claims).

We are OK with a narrow IP trigger (unmodified Service) but need the order form to explicitly call out customer-provided fine-tuning or prompt datasets as an area where Customer retains responsibility.

Next steps: provide Polaris' broker contact and we can schedule a 30-min call Tues 5/13 to finalize offset stacking mechanics. Please send your POI template and Kimberly's tracked redline in advance.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Head of Legal — Polaris Data
legal@polaris-data.com
Attachments referenced: Polaris will send broker contact (via separate email).
